newsitem.title: USA: Saudi bombing suspect may cooperate with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Saudi bombing suspect may cooperate with U.S..

text.p: A suspect held in Canada over a bomb attack that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia last June has expressed interest in cooperating with U.S. authorities, federal law enforcement officials said on Sunday.

The officials said the suspect, Hani Abdel Rahim Sayegh, who is being held in an Ottawa prison, would prefer to come to the United States rather than return to his native country of Saudi Arabia, where he fears torture and possible execution.
It will be up to Canada to decide where to send Sayegh.
The officials said Canadian officials would have another hearing in Sayegh's case on Tuesday, when a possible decision would be made.

U.S. official have sought to question Sayegh in connection with the June attack on the Khobar Towers compound that housed U.S. military personnel in Dhahran in eastern Saudi Arabia. The bombing killed 19 Americans and injured hundreds more.
Sayegh's Canadian lawyer, Doug Baum, could not be reached for comment, but previously has made known his client's strong preference to avoid deportation to Saudi Arabia.

Sayegh has been identified in Canadian court documents as the driver of a car that gave the go-ahead signal for the bomb-laden truck involved in the attack on Khobar Towers. He has denied any involvement and said he was in Syria at the time of the bombing.

If Sayegh comes to the United States, he would be the first witness the FBI has directly questioned in its probe of the Khobar Towers bombing. Saudi Arabia has refused to allowed U.S. officials direct access to any suspects or witnesses.
Justice Department officials said they are still reviewing legal options in the complicated case. They acknowledged they did not have enough evidence to charge Sayegh in connection with the bombing.

One possibility, they said, would be to have Sayegh arrested on a warrant as a "material witness" in the case, a seldom-used procedure that would allow authorities to hold Sayegh while they question him.
